transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Diana Moore (Redwood AE), Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AcceleraCloud Partnerships), Liam Chen (AcceleraCloud Cloud Solutions), Sanjay Patel (AcceleraCloud Network & Security)

Summary (auto-model): quick partner intro; focus on how Redwood can run on AcceleraCloud nodes and what the integration surface looks like.

00:00:07 - Diana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Diana from Redwood, AE on the partner motion, and with me is Carlos our SE.
00:00:15 - Priya: Thanks Diana, excited to learn more, I'm Priya, I run partnerships at AcceleraCloud.
00:00:22 - Carlos: quick context, Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and a Private deployment model for partner clouds — all same API surface but different infra tradeoffs.
00:00:38 - Liam: when you say Private, do you mean full control plane in our VPC or like a managed control plane with peering?
00:00:45 - Carlos: both options, we can do customer-managed control plane in your VPC for regulated workloads, or a peered model where the control plane is managed by Redwood but data channels stay private. there's some network reqs (ports, latency) — we'll share an ops doc.
00:01:02 - Sanjay: what about KMS/HSM for keys? we need to keep customer keys on our side.
00:01:08 - Diana: yes we support KMS integrations and in the private/on-prem model you can manage keys; for dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS via our connector.
00:01:20 - Priya: awesome — also compliance, most of our customers ask for SOC 2 and audit logs, do you capture token-level logs?
00:01:29 - Carlos: we do token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console, and we can provide audit logs; there are options to limit retention for privacy.
00:01:40 - Liam: cost is the big one — if we run H100s for low-latency chat that'll eat margins; do you recommend quantization?
00:01:49 - Carlos: yes, quant profiles and batching help; Redwood Optimize gives recommendations (quantize to 4-bit where acceptable), plus smart batching to improve throughput. we can model typical prompt distributions to estimate unit cost.
00:02:05 - Priya: are you tied to specific GPU types? our fleet is mixed A100 and H100.
00:02:10 - Carlos: we're hardware-agnostic largely, runtime will pick kernels; H100 gives perf ups for some models but costs more. we should run perf tests on both to show delta — i'll prepare a spreadsheet.
00:02:25 - Diana: as for go-to-market, some partners do referral fees, some do co-sell. what's your preference, Priya?
00:02:32 - Priya: open to both, depends on support load. we don't want to own a complex POC that costs us a ton.
00:02:40 - Sanjay: network details — peering vs private link? we prefer private link with enforced ACLs and no public egress for customer data.
00:02:48 - Carlos: PrivateLink-style setup is supported in our private offering; we'll need to validate ports and MTU. i'll ask for network diagrams.
00:02:58 - Liam: operationally how are upgrades handled? we run a lot of long-running KV cache sessions for chat.
00:03:06 - Carlos: the runtime handles KV cache and rolling updates, we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a model variant if something degrades. but for private installs we coordinate maintenance windows.
00:03:20 - Priya: typical timeline for a POC?
00:03:23 - Diana: usually 4-6 weeks from scoping to a small pilot depending on infra access and benchmarks. first phase is perf/cost benchmarking, then integration, then limited customer trial.
00:03:33 - Priya: okay, we'll need a clear SOW and E2E SLA numbers if we commit to co-sell.
00:03:39 - Diana: understood, we'll draft an initial SOW template and proposed SLAs.
00:03:45 - Liam: any references or customers running on partner clouds now?
00:03:49 - Diana: yes a few OEM partners and MSPs, i can share anonymized case studies; also a benchmark doc comparing A100/H100 for common models.
00:04:00 - Sanjay: security review — will you share SOC 2 report and pen test summary?
00:04:05 - Diana: yes i'll share our security package; Carlos will attach the integration checklist.
00:04:12 - Priya: there was a note about licensing for models — do you host open models or bring-your-own-model?
00:04:19 - Carlos: both. we host curated open models and you can bring your own model weights for private installs; we also support model pinning and versioned rollouts.
00:04:30 - Priya: great. any limitations on model size for Private?
00:04:33 - Carlos: no hard limits but you need the infra; for very large models we recommend sharded deployments and we'll help with the config.
00:04:42 - Liam: latency targets — can we expect sub-200ms for short prompts?
00:04:46 - Carlos: depends on model and batch size; with H100 and optimized kernels you'd maybe get low latency, but for determinism dedicated pools are better. we'll include target ranges in the perf estimate.
00:05:00 - Diana: okay to recap next steps — i'll send the partner one-pager, pricing tiers and security pack; carlos will spin up the benchmark plan; sanjay will share network and SOC/requirements.
00:05:12 - Priya: sounds good. we'll then schedule the technical deep dive/POC scoping with infra team.
00:05:18 - Diana: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings, some product names abbreviated (KV cache, PrivateLink), and speaker overlaps.

End of transcript.
